tools.name: post_message
tools.description: Post a one or two line chat message to the user. Pass file_name to link a file you registered with attach_file.

tools.name: remove_todo
tools.description: Remove a TODO this TODO created with create_todo, only when the user's instruction says to: like the user's Remove, its run stops and it moves to the Removed fold, where the user can restore it.

tools.name: set_schedule
tools.description: Set, change, pause or remove (schedule null) the schedule of a TODO this TODO created with create_todo, only when the user's instruction says to. schedule: {days: [1,2,3,4,5], times: ["09:00"]} or {days, every: 30, from: "08:00", to: "18:00"} (days 0 = Sunday, local time), optional prompt (each run's first message; left out, the TODO's first instruction) and paused.

tools.name: set_title
tools.description: Set this TODO's title: a short summary of the task.

tools.name: set_attention
tools.description: Raise the attention flag (raised: true) when you need the user; clear it (raised: false) once their reply resolves it.

tools.name: attach_file
tools.description: Register a file you wrote in this TODO's artifact folder (/tmp/sb-data/1) so the user can open it. Pass its absolute path.

tools.name: set_worktree
tools.description: Register the absolute path of the git worktree this TODO works in.

tools.name: set_pr
tools.description: Register the number of the GitHub pull request this TODO works on, in its topic's GitHub repository. The app shows its state, checks and reviews.

tools.name: set_effort
tools.description: Switch your effort level: low, medium, high or xhigh. reason: a few words the user reads, such as "verifying the fix". Refused when the user set the effort.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List the user's open comments on files of this TODO: each has the file's path, the line where the selected text started (when known), the selected text (quote), the comment, and your earlier reply if the user edited the comment after it. Answer each with reply_comment.

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: Reply to one of the user's comments from list_comments. You changed the file for it: start the reply with "Applied" and say what you changed in a few words. A question: answer it, no edit. Unclear: ask your question as the reply. The user resolves the comment or edits it to follow up.

tools.name: suggest_follow_ups
tools.description: Suggest one or two follow-ups the user can send you with a click, each one line written as their instruction to you (e.g. "Approve the PR"). A later call replaces the earlier ones.

tools.name: read_todo
tools.description: Read one TODO by its number (T-42 is 42), removed ones too: its details, its sessions with their chat messages, and its file list.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read one of a TODO's text files by its name: its attached markdown files and the user's uploads. For an image or other binary file it returns the path to open with Read.

tools.name: create_todo
tools.description: Create a TODO with its first instruction. title: a short title for its card; leave it out and the TODO's agent sets one. topic: one of Alpha, beta, or "none" for a thinking-only TODO; leave it out and routing picks it at the start. start: true starts it now, only when the user's words say to start it; otherwise it lands in the user's backlog. key: a dedupe key such as "pr:copilot-service#490"; when a TODO has that key already, removed ones too, nothing is created. schedule: {days: [1,2,3,4,5], times: ["09:00"]} or {days, every: 30, from: "08:00", to: "18:00"} (days 0 = Sunday, local time) makes a scheduled TODO that runs a new session at each slot; only when the user asks for one.

tools.name: route_todo
tools.description: Decide which topic this TODO belongs to: a topic's name, or "none" for a thinking-only TODO without a topic. The reason is one short sentence the user reads. effort: the level the TODO's agent starts at (low, medium, high, xhigh); leave it out for medium. Stop after this call.

tools.name: ask_topic
tools.description: Ask the user which topic this TODO belongs to, when you cannot tell: a short question and the 2 or 3 likely topics by name. The user also gets a "No topic" choice. Stop after this call.
